text:
Jordan: heads-up — our pre-merge SAST job is flaking on main. CI sometimes marks the step as 'skipped' and the PR gets merged. Started ~2h ago, maybe around the KMS rotation window.
Maria: saw that too. Logs show a decrypt error in the secrets step: `ERROR: gcloud kms decrypt: permission denied` then the scanner step exits 0 because we had skip_on_error: true.
sec-ci-bot: [ci-runner] workflow #2784 failed, jobs: sast_check (timed_out), re-run: https://ci.redwood.internal/runs/2784
Lee: quick theory — key rotated earlier and the IAM binding for the CI service account didn't reapply to the new key version. Cloud KMS rotation can create new keys with different resource ids.
Sophie: ugh. If scans are being skipped we lose gating guarantees. We shouldn't have skip_on_error for SAST/DAST. Fail closed until we have a safe fallback.
Jordan: Agreed. Proposed immediate actions: 1) reapply IAM binding to current key version, 2) update GH action to retry decrypt on transient errors, 3) remove skip_on_error for critical scans, 4) open SEC ticket to review rotation + audit logging. I'm doing 1 and 2 now.
Maria: +1. For 1 the command we used last time was:
```
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/ci-keys/cryptoKeys/sast-key \
  --member=serviceAccount:ci-runner@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter
```
Lee: also add the binding at the cryptoKeyVersion level if rotation created a new version ID. Example terraform snippet to make binding stable:
```
resource "google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member" "ci_decrypter" {
  crypto_key_id = "projects/${var.project}/locations/global/keyRings/ci-keys/cryptoKeys/sast-key"
  role          = "roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter"
  member        = "serviceAccount:ci-runner@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
}
```
Sophie: For medium term: consider using a dedicated service account + key that rotates on a controlled schedule and is owned by infra. And enable Data Access audit logs for Cloud KMS so we can trace decrypt calls. Retention suggestion: 365d for security-critical keys.
Jordan: I'll create the ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-1234 — notes: audit log enablement, rotation policy, RBAC tightening (least-privilege decrypt only), and runbook for broken decrypts.
Maria: Also check our Github Actions runner secret — we store encrypted scanner token in repo secrets and CI decrypts at runtime. If decrypt fails we should re-run automatically instead of skip. I'll open a small PR to add 3 retries with exponential backoff.
sec-ci-bot: [automation] created issue SEC-1234 and assigned to Jordan.
Lee: one more thing — our vulnerability triage flow: when a false negative/skip occurs, we should annotate the merged PR with a vuln-risk label and kick off a post-merge scan job that blocks deploy until resolved. That gives immediate visibility.
Sophie: +1. Also add a small endpoint in the console where infra can temporarily revoke the CI key (if compromised) and rotate without breaking gating — see runbook stub in the ticket.
Jordan: timeline: reapply IAM binding (done), push retry patch (in PR), remove skip_on_error in a follow-up PR (target: end of day). Will post updates here and in SEC-1234.
Maria: thanks — once PRs are up I'll do a quick review.
Sophie: can we also add an alert on >2 skipped/failed scans in a 1h window? Paging to sec-oncall if so.
Jordan: good idea. I'll add a Datadog monitor for `ci.sast.skips.count > 2` -> page sec-oncall.
Maria: FYI I confirmed decrypt errors correlate with KMS rotation timestamp in audit logs. After reapplying binding, a handful of jobs retried and succeeded.
Lee: long-term: document key rotation steps and add an integration test that simulates key rotation during a run.
Jordan: thanks team. Closing loop when SEC-1234 has the runbook and RBAC changes merged. :white_check_mark:
